title: The Seven Ravens
lines: Once there was a man who had seven sons.
This man always prayed that God would bless him with a little daughter too.
God heard his many prayers, and gave him a lovely little baby girl.
But the little girl was so weak when she was born
that they feared she would not live even one day.
Quickly they sent the seven sons to fetch fresh spring water from the forest,
to christen the child with it, so that she would not die unchristened.
The boys ran into the forest, but when they reached the spring,
each wanted to be the first to fill the jug, and the jug fell into the well.
In it went, and because the well was deep, they could not get the jug out.
The poor boys were sad, not knowing what to do now.
They did not dare go home, so they stayed in the forest,
and their father could not imagine what had happened to them.
- They must have started playing, he said, and forgotten all about the water.
Still the boys did not come, and their father grew angrier and angrier.
In his great anger,
that now the little girl would die unchristened, he began to curse:
- I wish all seven of them would turn into ravens!
The words had hardly left his mouth when he heard loud chattering and cawing.
The man looked up, and there were seven black ravens flying above him.
Oh, dear God, a great heavy sorrow fell upon the man's heart,
and an even greater one upon his wife's heart.
They wept and wailed and tore their hair, but no matter: their sons stayed ravens.
Still, they were lucky that the little girl did not die,
but grew stronger and prettier from day to day.
For a long time the little girl did not know that she had brothers,
but one day she happened to hear from the neighbours
that she had had seven brothers and they had become ravens because of her.
Oh, dear God, how sad this made the little girl!
She ran to her father and mother and asked:
- Is it true, my dear parents, that I had seven brothers?
Where are they, what became of them?
- Well, there is no denying it, said her father, you had seven brothers,
but the poor boys were turned into ravens when you were born.
We will weep for them until we die.
From that moment on the little girl had no peace.
She felt her brothers became ravens because of her, and she made a vow -
come what may -
that she would not rest
until she had found her brothers and freed them from the curse.
She told her parents what she meant to do,
but oh, how they wept and wailed then!
Was it not enough that they had lost seven dear, handsome sons,
must they now lose their only daughter too?
But all their weeping was in vain, the little girl could not stay at home.
She had a little ring her parents had given her to remember them, she took only that,
and a piece of bread and a jug of water: and so she set out into the world.
On and on went the little girl, over hills and valleys, through forest
and across fields, on and on she went, until she came to the very end of the world.
But there at the end of the world the sun shone so hot
that the little girl ran on in terror: she thought she would burn to ashes on the spot.
She ran to the moon, but it was so cold that she nearly froze.
The poor thing ran on in a panic and did not stop until she reached the stars.
They twinkled and smiled so kindly, sat her down among them, and asked what she wanted,
how she had come here, and when she told them
that she was looking for her brothers, the Evening Star said:
- Well, you have come to the right place, little girl.
Your seven brothers are on the Ice Mountain.
Here, I will give you a little key,
with it you will open the Ice Mountain gate, and there you will find your brothers.
She thanked them nicely for the gift,
said goodbye to the stars, and ran up the Ice Mountain like the swift wind.
At the top she looked and looked for the key to open the door, but could not find it.
Oh, dear God, what could she do now?
How could she free her brothers?
She thought and thought, then took her little knife and cut off her little finger,
put it into the gate, and look, at that very moment it opened.
She went through the gate, but after two steps a dwarf stood before her and asked:
- What are you looking for here, little girl?
The little girl answered:
- I am looking for my brothers, the seven ravens, dear dwarf.
Are they here?
- Here, yes, said the dwarf, but they are not at home just now.
But if you want to wait for them until they come home, then come in.
They went into the seven ravens' room, and there the dwarf laid the table,
set out seven plates, seven cups, food on all seven plates, drink in all seven cups.
The little girl tasted the food of all seven, one by one,
she ate a little from each of the seven plates,
she drank from the cups too, and into the last cup she dropped her ring.
All at once the little girl heard a great flapping of wings
and cawing, and the dwarf announced:
- Now, little girl, here come the raven lords!
And in came the ravens, flying through the door,
they sat down at the table and began to eat,
but they saw at once that someone had eaten their food and drunk their drink.
- Who has eaten and who has drunk here? they asked each other.
It was a person, that is certain.
Then the youngest raven happened to look at the bottom of his cup, and saw the ring.
- Look, a ring! he cried.
This was our parents' ring!
Look!
- So it is!
This is our parents' ring! they all cried in great wonder.
- Oh, dear God, said the eldest,
if only our little sister were here, we would be freed from the curse at once!
At that very moment the little girl ran out from behind the door, where she had hidden,
and, hear this wonder, the seven ravens turned into boys at once!
And what handsome boys they were!
One by one they hugged and kissed the little girl, then without
a word more they set off home, and did not stop until they got there.
And then at home!
That was where the real joy was!
They are all still alive today, if they have not died.
